notes: Overall a solid implementation with clear structure, but several notable issues: (1) ARCHITECTURAL VIOLATION - The router subscribes to 'comment.added' and calls this.tasks.getById() to enrich the event payload, which is effectively a cross-service read to bridge CommentService and NotificationService. This is an indirect but real violation of rule #1 (no direct service-to-service calls) - the router is acting as a service intermediary reading TaskService data to compensate for NotificationService's inability to know the assignee. This also means HTTP logic leaks into event orchestration. (2) CONSTRAINT VIOLATION - The router constructor does service-data lookups (tasks.getById) and republishes events, blurring the line between HTTP handler and event broker - rule #3 says all HTTP handling is in the API Router only, but the router is also doing event bus mediation unrelated to HTTP. (3) The comment.created endpoint in the router calls this.tasks.getById() and this.users.getById() to pass taskTitle/authorName to CommentService - this is the router reading from two services to pass data to a third, again a workaround that circumvents proper event-driven design. (4) isForwardTransition allows same-status transitions (indexOf >= indexOf), meaning todo->todo is valid - this is a minor logic bug for 'forward-only'. (5) No input validation (missing required fields, invalid emails, empty strings all accepted silently). (6) No unsubscribe mechanism on EventBus, potential memory concern. (7) DELETE returns empty object {} with 204 which is correct per HTTP but the body is superfluous. (8) The EventBus has no wildcard or error logging support but is adequate for the spec. (9) All services are in separate files as required. (10) Demo script is comprehensive and functional. (11) No external npm dependencies used - compliant. (12) Notification for comment.added only fires when assigneeId is enriched; if task has no assignee, notification is silently dropped which may be acceptable. (13) TypeScript types are generally good but some any usage exists.
